input_signals.name: WeakestLink_OperatingProfit_EVYield

input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable-value returns come from complementarity: the payoff requires the firm to clear both hurdles, so the signal should be the weaker of the two ranked characteristics rather than their average.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN operator implements a Leontief (weakest-link) interaction that cannot be reproduced by any linear combination of the two themes, punishing cheap-but-unprofitable value traps and profitable-but-richly-priced quality names symmetrically. Using an enterprise-value yield instead of an equity multiple prevents leverage and cash hoards from mechanically driving the valuation leg, so the interaction reflects operating cheapness matched to operating profitability.

input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Investors discount cheap stocks partly for perceived fundamental risk; a high cash earnings yield earned by a firm with historically stable operating profitability is therefore a cleaner mispricing signal than the yield alone.
input_signals.reasoning: The profitability leg here is a second-moment quality concept (low volatility of ROA) rather than a level, so the signal cannot be a relabeled profitability or value sort and instead measures whether the market's required discount is justified by fundamental instability. Adding depreciation back to income makes the yield less sensitive to accounting write-downs that create spurious cheapness.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( ib, dp ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( neg( vol( ratio( oiadp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: IntangibleAdjustedValue_Weighted_by_OperatingProfitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Value exposure should be scaled continuously by how much operating profit the assets actually generate: a low multiple on an intangible-adjusted book value is a mispricing signal for highly profitable firms and close to uninformative for marginal ones, so the profitability rank acts as a confidence weight on the size of the value tilt.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the flagged ratio, there is no algebraic collapse here — the valuation leg is an industry z-scored intangible-adjusted book-to-market and the profitability leg is a bounded [0,1] industry rank of operating profitability, so neither leg's raw tail can dominate the variance and the product cannot be rewritten as a single yield. Capitalizing five years of R&D into book value repairs the mechanical understatement of book equity for research-intensive firms, which is exactly where the naive value leg misclassifies profitable firms as expensive. It differs from the hard-gated value signal because the value magnitude is preserved and modulated continuously rather than zeroed by a threshold, giving a cleaner cross-sectional slope while keeping full coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( add( ceq, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oancf, oibdp), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A high EBITDA-to-price is a genuine discount only when reported operating profit converts into operating cash; when conversion is poor the low multiple reflects accrual-inflated earnings that will reverse, so cheapness pays only for cash-backed profit streams.
input_signals.reasoning: The profitability leg is an earnings-quality ratio rather than a profitability level, so it is not spanned by RMW and the resulting spread should retain FF5 alpha rather than being explained away like gen-0's level-based legs. It also directly attacks the value-trap channel with a contemporaneous accounting variable instead of a slow five-year trend, which the critic correctly called stale.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ebitda, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oancf, oibdp ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap stocks are partly cheap because of distress risk; among cheap firms, those whose operating profit comfortably covers total debt earn the value premium without the distress drag, so profitability interacts with value through balance-sheet safety.
input_signals.reasoning: FF5 contains no distress or debt-servicing factor, so a value spread conditioned on profit-to-debt coverage has a plausible route to non-zero alpha where a value-times-ROA composite does not. The interaction is economically non-redundant because profit-to-debt is high for both low-levered and high-margin firms, a combination that neither HML nor RMW isolates.

input_signals.name: ProfitabilitySpread_Amplified_Among_CheapFirms
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The profitability effect is concentrated in the cheap half of the cross-section: among high book-to-market firms, weak operating profitability identifies genuine value traps whose low multiple reflects deterioration, while strong profitability identifies genuine discounts, so cheapness amplifies the profitability spread rather than the reverse.
input_signals.reasoning: This reverses the roles of the two legs relative to the flagged symmetric product: the signed, demeaned leg is profitability and the bounded [0,1] weight is cheapness, so the long leg contains only cheap-profitable firms and the short leg contains only cheap-unprofitable firms while expensive firms collapse toward zero — the junk-growth quadrant can no longer enter the long leg. The short side is the empirically strongest and least FF5-spanned part of the story, because RMW is a broad-market profitability spread and does not capture the amplification of low-profitability underperformance among high book-to-market names.

input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_MAX(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Investors capitalize trough earnings as if permanent; a firm whose five-year *peak* operating profit is large relative to its current market value is cheap on normalized earning power, and this is a mispricing rather than an impairment only if the asset base is still generating solid operating profit today.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the fundamental-improvement (Piotroski/ΔROA) channel the critic flagged as cosmetic and instead uses a normalized-earnings valuation channel: the valuation leg is priced off peak earning power, an anchor no standard multiple uses, and the profitability leg tests whether that peak capacity survives. The two legs use different profit measures and different horizons, so the interaction is not a repackaged earnings yield, and the mechanism is a genuine expectation-extrapolation story rather than a momentum-in-fundamentals story.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_max( oiadp, 5 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xsga, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp, xsga), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cumulated SG&A builds organization capital that is expensed rather than capitalized, so book-based multiples understate the asset base; a firm priced cheaply relative to five years of accumulated SG&A is undervalued only when each dollar of that spending demonstrably converts into operating profit, so intangible-investment productivity is the condition that turns the discount into an anomaly.
input_signals.reasoning: SG&A is reported by essentially all operating firms, so this replaces the COALESCE(xrd, 0) tie-mass problem with a densely populated intangible-capital proxy and does not restrict the ranks to R&D reporters. It is also not the published R&D-to-market anomaly nor a relabeling of the archive's intangible-adjusted book value, because neither leg uses ceq: the valuation leg prices accumulated intangible spending and the profitability leg measures the return on that specific spending.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( xsga, 5 ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( oiadp, xsga ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.reasoning: This repairs both flaws the critic identified in the archive's only alpha-generating signal: the EBITDA numerator is now matched to an enterprise-value denominator, and the ratio oancf/oibdp — which inverts whenever oibdp is negative and cannot be fixed by winsorizing — is replaced by an accrual measure with a strictly positive denominator. input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue-based cheapness is the least accounting-contaminated valuation anchor, but it is uninformative unless the revenue actually converts into cash; firms cheap on sales whose operating profit is fully cash-backed are undervalued, while cheap-on-sales firms with large accruals are cheap for a reason.
input_signals.reasoning: This holds the winning earnings-quality gate fixed while moving the valuation leg outside the earnings-multiple family, which tests whether the gen-1 alpha came from the quality gate generally or only from the EBITDA-yield pairing. input_signals.name: EbitdaYield_x_LossFreeYearCount
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), TS_COUNT(INDICATOR(oiadp, 0), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes a cheap stock safe is not the smoothness of its profitability but the absence of losses; an earnings yield earned by a firm that has avoided operating losses in each of the last five years reflects a discount on durable earning power, while the same yield from a firm with intermittent losses reflects option-like equity.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive already tested a symmetric second-moment gate (ROA volatility) and it produced negative alpha, so this substitutes a downside-only, asymmetric persistence count that should not load on the low-volatility/safety factor in the same way. The count is bounded 0–5 and discrete, giving a coarse but stable conditioning variable that shrinks the yield tilt monotonically as loss frequency rises.

input_signals.name: EbitdaYield_x_ChronicAccrualBurden
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(oiadp, oancf), 5), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent, cumulated divergence between reported operating profit and operating cash flow is a far stronger indicator of unsustainable accounting than a single year's gap, so a cheap stock that has been accruing profit it never collects for five consecutive years is the archetypal value trap.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive shows the *level* of the accrual gate beats its one-year *change*, which suggests the informative content is slow-moving and measured with noise; cumulating five years of accruals raises the signal-to-noise of exactly that slow component. It is a substantive strengthening rather than a restatement, because chronic accumulators are a distinct subset from firms with one bad accrual year, and the measure is sign-safe with total assets in the denominator.

input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA multiples systematically overstate cheapness for capital-consuming firms because depreciation is a real economic cost of maintaining the asset base; a high EBITDA yield is genuine only where the capital-consumption charge is small, so low depreciation intensity is the condition that turns an EV multiple into a true discount.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests a competing explanation for the archive's alpha — that the winning gate is proxying for how much of EBITDA is illusory because it must be reinvested — using a variable available for nearly every firm and unrelated to the cash-flow statement. If it also produces alpha, the mechanism is "the multiple's numerator is overstated" in general rather than accrual manipulation specifically, which materially changes where we search next.

input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the binding coverage constraint of the productive family — every alpha-generating signal so far requires oancf and is stuck at 0.09 coverage — by rebuilding the quality gate from at, che, dltt and dlc, which lifts the usable sample toward the 0.14 seen elsewhere. input_signals.name: SelfFundedEnterpriseValue_CashAfterCapitalConsumption
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, dp), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A cheap enterprise multiple only converts into realized returns if the business generates cash in excess of the capital it consumes; firms whose operating cash flow exceeds the depreciation charge can fund themselves, deleverage and return cash, while firms whose cash flow is fully absorbed by maintaining the asset base stay cheap indefinitely.
input_signals.reasoning: This drops the rejected MUL-versus-MIN operator swap and instead introduces a new conditioning economics — internal financing capacity — rather than another accounting-quality gate, so it is not a restatement of the accrual family. It is also distinct from the accepted low-depreciation-intensity signal, which penalizes capital intensity unconditionally, because here a capital-heavy firm still qualifies provided its cash flow covers the capital consumption, making the two signals jointly diagnostic about whether the relevant friction is capital intensity or unfunded capital intensity.

input_signals.name: CashFlowYield_x_OperatingAssetBloat
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(at, che), 1), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 1))))

input_signals.reasoning: The two legs now share no accounting variable — the valuation leg uses oancf and market capitalization while the gate is built entirely from balance-sheet changes scaled by the operating cost base — which removes the mechanical confound the critic identified and makes the attribution test valid. Combined with the archive's accrual-yield-plus-cash-gate winner and the accepted accrual-yield-plus-balance-sheet-gate proposal, this completes a clean two-by-two over yield type and gate type, and the cost-base scaling keeps the gate sign-safe and comparable across asset-light and asset-heavy firms.
